title: How Much Car Can You Really Afford? (The 20/4/10 Math)

lines.say: How much car can you afford?
The dealer will ask what monthly payment you want. Here's the math to answer with instead.
A common guideline is called twenty, four, ten.

items: A loan of 4 years or less
All car costs under 10% of gross pay

lines.cap: 20% down. A loan of 4 years or less. And total car costs under 10% of your gross income.
lines.say: Twenty percent down. A loan of four years or less. And total car costs under ten percent of your gross income.
Let's run it for our example. Sixty thousand a year.

scene.label: 10% of $5,000 a month
scene.sub: for the payment, insurance, gas and upkeep, all of it

lines.cap: $60,000 a year is $5,000 a month, gross. 10% is $500, for everything car-related.
lines.say: Sixty thousand a year is five thousand a month, gross. Ten percent is five hundred dollars, for everything car-related.

lines.cap: Now subtract the costs that aren't the payment. $500. Minus insurance, $140. Minus gas, $120. Minus upkeep, $40.
lines.say: Now subtract the costs that aren't the payment. Five hundred. Minus insurance, one forty. Minus gas, one twenty. Minus upkeep, forty.

lines.cap: That leaves $200 a month for the payment.
lines.say: That leaves two hundred dollars a month for the payment.

scene.label: $200/mo · 4 years · 7% · 20% down
scene.sub: car price that fits the rule on $60,000

lines.cap: At 7% over four years, $200 a month borrows about $8,350. With 20% down, that's a car around $10,440.
lines.say: At seven percent over four years, two hundred a month borrows about eighty-three fifty. With twenty percent down, that's a car around ten thousand, four hundred.

lines.cap: $30,000 borrowed at 7%. Over four years, the payment is $718.
lines.say: Thirty thousand borrowed at seven percent. Over four years, the payment is seven eighteen.

lines.cap: Stretch it to six years and the payment drops to $511. It feels cheaper. But you pay $6,826 in interest instead of $4,483.
lines.say: Stretch it to six years, and the payment drops to five eleven. It feels cheaper. But you pay sixty-eight twenty-six in interest instead of forty-four eighty-three.

scene.text: Asked for a monthly payment? Answer with a total price.

lines.say: So when the dealer asks what payment you want, answer with a total price.

scene.label: Our example from episode one
scene.sub: of gross pay on the car: a little over the line

lines.cap: And our example from episode one? Car payment $340, insurance $140, gas and upkeep about $160. $640 a month: 12.8% of gross.
lines.say: And our example from episode one? Car payment three forty, insurance one forty, gas and upkeep about one sixty. Six forty a month. Twelve point eight percent of gross.
A little over the line. Not a disaster, but it's why the next car should be cheaper, or paid for longer before it's replaced.
